quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: How should a rider sit to best control a motorcycle?

options.text: Using arms to hold their body up
With knees away from the gas tank
With feet firmly on the footrests

questions.correctAnswerText: With feet firmly on the footrests
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not hold you up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet firmly on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver is following you too closely?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass
questions.explanation: Get the tailgating driver in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up may only cause them to tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever located on a motorcycle?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: What happens if your front tire goes flat while riding?

options.text: The steering will feel the same
The ride will feel too smooth

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering will feel heavy
questions.explanation: A flat front tire causes heavy steering. If your steering feels heavy, exit the road right away and check your tires.

questions.question: Where should you look when turning on a motorcycle?

options.text: Close to the front of the motorcycle
Through the turn to where you want to go
Turn your entire body to see through the turn
Increase your speed before the turn

questions.correctAnswerText: Through the turn to where you want to go
questions.explanation: Look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Which action should you NOT take to improve safety when riding at night?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight when possible

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your speed
questions.explanation: Ride safely at night by reducing speed, using your high beam headlight when not near other vehicles, and increasing following distance. Watch vehicles ahead of you—their headlights show the road ahead, and their taillights bounce if hitting bumps.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective riding gear?
questions.correctAnswerText: Pants made of soft material
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a jacket and pants made of leather or sturdy material, boots that cover and support your ankles, and hearing protection even with a helmet.

questions.question: How do you lean a motorcycle to turn?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn
Press the handgrip opposite to the turn direction

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn to make this happen.

questions.question: How much stopping power does the front brake provide?
questions.correctAnswerText: About three-quarters
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Which option provides the best face protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield that does not shatter protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield does not provide enough protection.

questions.question: What can a shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Protect a rider's face in a crash.
Should not be used with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect a rider's face in a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes, not your whole face. A face shield also protects you from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and pebbles.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist tell a passenger to do?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Get on the motorcycle after the engine is started.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on the motorcycle after the engine is started.
questions.explanation: Give your passenger safety instructions before the trip. Have them get on after you start the engine. They should sit as close to you as comfortable and hold your waist, hips, or belt. They should keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can affect a rider?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can affect your ability to ride. Riding while under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Why check your motorcycle before riding?

options.text: It is useless unless done by a mechanic.
You should not do it before a ride.
You should only do it after a ride.
It helps find mechanical problems and equipment failures.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps find mechanical problems and equipment failures.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This helps you find mechanical problems or equipment failures that could be dangerous.

questions.question: How should you adjust for a passenger's weight?

options.text: Keep a shorter distance behind other vehicles.
Brake later than you normally would.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight. Your motorcycle needs more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Reduce your speed, start braking earlier, increase your distance from other vehicles, and leave bigger gaps when entering traffic.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a motorcycle horn?

options.text: Other drivers usually cannot hear it.
It can quickly get someone's attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can quickly get someone's attention.
questions.explanation: Your horn can help get someone's attention quickly. However, a motorcycle horn is not as loud as a car horn, so other drivers may not hear it. Never rely only on your horn to handle a hazard.

questions.question: What is the best sitting position on a motorcycle?

options.text: One where your arms hold you up.
One where you can easily reach the controls.
One where your arms are straight reaching the grips.
One where your knees are away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: One where you can easily reach the controls.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms steer the bike, not hold you up. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.

questions.question: A person drank 8 drinks 4 hours ago. How many drinks likely remain in their body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four drinks
questions.explanation: The body eliminates about one drink per hour. Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. In this case, 8 drinks minus 4 hours equals about 4 drinks remaining.

questions.question: When should reflective clothing be worn?
questions.correctAnswerText: Day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective materials at all times to increase your visibility.

questions.question: What does eye contact from another driver mean?

options.text: It does not mean they will yield to you.
It guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume a driver will yield just because they made eye contact. Drivers often look directly at a motorcyclist but do not consciously notice them.
